design_condition: The compact three-block volume is placed north of the site between existing buildings, relating to the surrounding geometries while forming a campus square and reserve spaces toward the south and west.

positive.statement: The project offers an interesting reading of the site and the program.
The jury appreciates the compactness and articulation of the project.
The wood-concrete hybrid construction is appreciated.
The large spans offer great flexibility in the organization of plans.
The proposal integrates sustainable-development principles well and could achieve the 200-watt society principles.

negative.statement: The number of meeting, free-work and relaxation spaces may be insufficient.
Access to the nursery terrace by a single elevator and emergency stairs is not convincing.
The nursery terrace as its unique outdoor space is controversially discussed.
The constrained situation limits the potential for expansion of the HES and the hospital's central functions.
The removal of approximately 115 parking spaces is not compensated.
The current logistics output appears modified and requires special attention in further development.
The transitions between the upper and lower floor typologies are not yet mastered, with significant load-transfer problems in the central part.
The expression remains somewhat subject to the constructive constraints of wood.
The complexity of three nested volumes would better highlight its qualities at a larger scale.
The facade development is relatively important and network and logistics relocations will generate significant transfer costs.
